text: Cures acne in 7 days. Guaranteed clear skin.
rationale: Therapeutic claim on a cosmetic. Reclassifies the product into drug licensing it does not hold.

text: India's #1 Niacinamide serum. The best formula money can buy.
rationale: Ranking and superlative claims with no cited substantiation. Requires published criteria per the ASCI awards guideline.
Fabricated concentration. The product is 10%. Layer 2, requires ProductFacts context.

text: Your skin is aging faster than you think. Don't wait until it's too late.
rationale: Fear-based framing. Persuasion mechanism is anxiety, not information. Layer 2.
Leucoderma is in the D&MR Act 1954 Schedule, so this engages s.3(d) directly. Live exposure for a brightening product line.

text: Fades dark spots permanently. Say goodbye to pigmentation for good.
rationale: Permanence claim, unsubstantiable for a topical cosmetic.

text: 10% Vitamin C + Glutathione Brightening Serum | Glow in 3 Days*
rationale: Real Foxtale copy. Quantified time-bound efficacy claim with no subject count, duration or source. The asterisk is doing work no disclosure follows up on.

text: actively prevents breakouts so you can bid adieu to acne & blemishes for good
Asia's 1st brand with made safe certified products.
rationale: Real Mamaearth copy. Ranking claim requiring published criteria and an independence undertaking.

text: Nothing else worked on my pimples and marks except this serum
rationale: Real The Derma Co testimonial. Absolute claim in a customer's voice. Layer 2.

text: 93% subjects saw significant reduction in active acne in 4 weeks
rationale: Real Minimalist copy. Quantified claim that carries its subject count and duration. This is what compliant strong copy looks like and it must not be flagged.
Real Minimalist copy, near-identical to The Derma Co's. The collision that disproves a claim-strength rule. Unquantified, so POLICY-003 does not apply.

text: ~26% more hydration than the benchmark product
rationale: Real Minimalist copy. Deliberately flags the brand's own live copy: unnamed comparative under ASCI 4.1(a), plus an approximation on a quantified claim.

text: Best used at night, after cleansing.
rationale: Adverbial 'best', not a superlative claim. POLICY-004's matcher must not fire on this.

text: Treats your skin to a lightweight layer of hydration.
rationale: 'Treats' in its non-medical sense. POLICY-001's matcher must not fire on this.

text: 10% Niacinamide. Helps reduce the appearance of blemishes over 8 weeks of regular use.
rationale: Reads claim-heavy but is hedged, states a real concentration, and gives a timeframe.

text: Formulated with 2% Salicylic Acid, printed on the front of every pack.
rationale: Contains a percentage that must be checked against ProductFacts rather than flagged on sight.

text: Thoroughly tested by an independent lab and confirmed SPF of 50 was obtained.
rationale: Real Minimalist copy. A quantified claim that names its source. Exactly what POLICY-003 is designed to permit.

text: This serum is good for oily skin and works well under makeup.
rationale: Contains 'good for', adjacent to POLICY-008's 'for good'. Ordering trap for the permanence matcher.
